title: Client reconciliation choiceboard and evidence bundle
content:
Summary:
On 2026-06-12 at approximately 03:12 UTC we detected an intermittent inference delivery anomaly that affected a small subset of requests routed through our eu-central-1 serving clusters. The root cause was a timing interaction between a rolling routing policy update and an async cache compaction process. The behavior resulted in a limited set of in-flight requests being reprocessed and, in some cases, returning outputs that included stale cache state fragments. Redwood stabilized the cluster configuration within 18 minutes and has implemented a temporary guard to prevent re-enqueue during cache compaction.

Scope and impact (plain terms):
- Affected window: 2026-06-12 03:08:51 UTC to 2026-06-12 03:26:30 UTC.
- Estimated affected calls: 0.4% of calls on impacted routing paths; impact concentrated on tenants using model alias rwd-chat-tiny with legacy-kv-enabled flag.
- Customer-observable symptoms: duplicated messages, truncated conversation turns, or occasional older context appearing in outputs for requests issued in the window.
- Severity: low-to-medium for customer-facing services; high-priority for internal integrity tracking.

Actions completed by Redwood (operational):
- Reverted the rolling routing update and deployed a fix to routing evaluation logic (complete).
- Disabled cache compaction trigger during active routing transitions (temporary guard, complete).
- Tagged and exported server-side artifacts for all requests in the window (request ids, timestamps, raw responses, routing traces) and stored them in an immutable audit store (in progress; will be finalized within 36 hours).
- Began assembling tenant-specific evidence bundles for delivery (in progress).

What we will deliver to each impacted tenant (evidence bundle):
- Secure archive containing: an index of impacted request ids, original request payloads (PII trimmed by default), original responses, server decision traces (routing and cache events), operator logs that show the rollback and fix, and cryptographic hashes for each artifact.
- A short reconciliation summary that highlights likely duplicates and a preliminary equivalence score for each request (automated heuristic).
- A small verification helper (shell + python) and checksums to let tenant engineers validate the artifact integrity locally.
- Delivery channel: pre-signed s3 link sent to tenant admin email on file; additional SFTP or direct share available on request.

Tenant choiceboard (options explained):
Option 1 — Full automated reconciliation (recommended for customers who prefer low-touch):
- Redwood will automatically replay all impacted requests in a controlled replay environment against the tenant's current pinned model variant, compare outputs to originals using deterministic runs where possible, and produce a reconciliation report. Where outputs are judged equivalent by our automated checks, Redwood will update the tenant's long-term response store to replace corrected outputs. For non-equivalent cases, we will surface diffs to tenant reviewers.
- Expected duration: 48	60 hours after tenant opt-in.
- Tenant action: approve via reply, or toggle the reconciliation setting in Console > Incidents > Pending Actions.

Option 2 — Assisted targeted replay (preferred for customers who want control):
- Redwood provides the full bundle and an indexed list of high-risk request ids. Tenant chooses a subset for targeted replay; Redwood performs those replays, returns diffs and contextual notes, and helps with manual reconciliation suggestions.
- Expected duration: proof bundle delivered in 48 hours; targeted replays scheduled 2	5 business days after request.
- Tenant action: reply with selection of request ids or time ranges to replay.

Option 3 — Audit-only delivery + service credit (fastest path, minimal operational change):
- Tenant receives the evidence bundle and a short audit note. Tenant declines replays. Redwood issues a one-time invoice credit proportional to verified affected calls. Replays remain available on-demand for 90 days.
- Expected duration: proof bundle delivered in 48 hours; credit applied on next billing cycle.
- Tenant action: reply to accept the credit and decline replays.

How we calculate credits (summary):
- Credit = impacted_calls_for_tenant * unit_call_rate * adjustment_factor. The adjustment factor accounts for our remediation effort; default factor = 1.2. Exact per-call rates reflect the tenant's billing plan and will be shown in the credit offer.

Verification steps (what tenants can run):
- Included in the bundle: verify.sh and verify_hashes.py. Basic flow:
  1) Download archive via pre-signed link.
  2) Run: ./verify.sh bundle.tar.gz (this checks signature and extracts).
  3) python verify_hashes.py bundle/index.json (recomputes SHA256 and compares).
- We will include example output diffs and a small guide for interpreting the equivalence score.

Data privacy and PII handling:
- Default delivery redacts or replaces high-sensitivity fields in request payloads. If a tenant requires full, unredacted payloads for forensic reasons, we will obtain explicit authorization and log the access event.

Default timeline and non-response policy:
- Redwood will deliver the evidence bundle to tenant contacts within 48 hours.
- If the tenant does not respond within 14 calendar days, Redwood will automatically apply Option 3 (audit-only + credit) and hold artifacts for 90 days for potential future replays.

Escalation and contact details:
- Primary contact: Luca Morales (luca.morales@redwood.ai).
- CS escalation alias: cs-escalations@redwood.ai.
- For legal or billing questions: legal-ops@redwood.ai and billing@redwood.ai.

Notes for internal reviewers:
- Confirm the wording of the non-response default period and whether 14 days aligns with enterprise contracts.
- Confirm credit multiplier and rounding rules with finance before finalizing the external note.

Draft history:
- 2026-06-14 initial draft (Luca).
- 2026-06-15 updates to wording and timelines (Aisha).

Attachments to include when sending to tenants: verification helper scripts, sample index.json schema, sample reconciliation report, and a short FAQ (why replays may differ; how to request unredacted payloads).
